newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper says bomb nearly hit his plane.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper says bomb nearly hit his plane.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper said on Thursday that he had survived a possible assassination attempt involving an attack on his presidential jet.

Samper, speaking in a Reuter interview, said the attempt involved a 44 pound (20 kg) bomb that exploded near the runway of the airport in Colombia's Caribbean port of Barranquilla, minutes before the presidential aircraft was due to land there on Wednesday.
Initial reports said the bomb had exploded up to 2.5 miles (4 km) from the airport runway and represented no real threat to Samper's Dutch-made Fokker aircraft.
But Samper said it exploded "just a few metres (yards) away from the head of the runway" and had apparently been intended to detonate just as the plane passed over it.

An air force official, hearing Samper's account, said he was lucky the device went off while the plane was still a good distance from the runway. The explosion, and resulting vacuum, could easily have destabilized the aircraft and caused it to crash, the official said.
"It's possible," Samper said when asked if he thought someone had tried to assassinate him. "But it's something it's best not to speculate about."
